svg.title: Delegated biometric authentication
svg.desc: You delegate your face to a register and a gate from your phone; later you show your face with no phone and no card, and the reader verifies a short-lived proof while the template stays on the phone
svg.text: Delegated biometric authentication
Your phone vouches for you at the register and the gate — without your face ever leaving it
You grant a delegation per reader, from the phone
Long-press an app, switch on "Require Face ID" — the same gesture, extended from apps to readers
Each grant names the reader and the purpose, expires, and can be withdrawn at any time
You walk up — no phone, no card
Point of sale
Look at the reader
Phone stays in your pocket
Apartment gate
No key, no card, no phone
Resident's face is never stored
The reader verifies a proof, not a face
Checks the face live, detects a photo or a mask
Sends a challenge; the phone answers from secure hardware
Verifies a short-lived signed statement
No template, no reusable image, no replay
The template never leaves the phone
The phone holds the biometric in secure hardware; the reader holds only a public key and a proof
The operator holds a delegation identifier and a log. Nobody holds a face — so nothing permanent is stolen
One open standard, one neutral trust service
The same grant, proof, verification and revocation rules work for every phone, reader and operator
Where identity is not needed, an unlinkable single-use token keeps the reader from tracking repeat visits
